signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows JPY outperforming all peers with a 1W average of +1.526% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags the complex at -1.027% across 4 pairs. This generates an extreme leader-to-laggard bilateral spread of 2.553%. Geopolitical disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude testing $100 reinforce defensive flows into JPY crosses. Meanwhile, the RBNZ cash rate of 2.75% provides only a 175bp nominal buffer against the BoJ rate of 1.0%, leaving NZD vulnerable as high-beta sentiment deteriorates. NZD/JPY trades at a sharp BEER-model discount of z=-3.29σ, reflecting intense short-term divergence. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by broad JPY outperformance and high-beta commodity currency liquidation. Catalyst: RBNZ policy meeting on 28 Oct — hold bias priced. Risk: Strait of Hormuz tensions de-escalate, prompting a sharp rebound in risk appetite and compression of the bilateral gap below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.28, holding below its technical SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.45/160.16/158.43. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY at -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18), marking an extreme positioning deficit that faces rapid liquidation. The 1M 25d risk reversal sits at -2.46, indicating heavy institutional demand for downside puts. Although the Fed rate of 3.75% versus BoJ 1.0% yields a 275bp policy rate advantage for USD, spot is divorcing from carry amid hawkish BoJ rate hike expectations and safe-haven rotation. USD/JPY 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 10.6% against 30-day realized volatility of 11.3%, leaving the volatility risk premium at -0.7%. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; crowded speculative shorts face ongoing squeeze pressure toward 150.00. Catalyst: BoJ policy meeting on 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Leveraged Funds rebuild JPY short exposure alongside a sustained daily close back above the 200-day SMA at 158.43.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long vs Retail Short
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7224, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7151/0.7054/0.6995. Leveraged Funds positioning reflects an overextended profile with net longs at +50,250 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.79), in the 94th percentile of its 52-week range. Conversely, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 91% short, establishing a stark institutional-versus-retail divergence. The RBA rate of 4.35% versus Fed 3.75% secures a 60bp cash carry premium for AUD, reinforced by an Australian Economic Surprise Index of +17.3. However, Saxo Bank 1M ATM implied volatility of 7.2% against 5.9% realized generates a +1.2% vol risk premium, showing that options markets are pricing upside exhaustion. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD, but crowded institutional positioning warns of late-trend stalling near 0.7300. Catalyst: RBA policy decision on 29 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: Leveraged Funds weekly net delta contracts sharply, triggering long liquidation toward the 20-day SMA at 0.7151.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CB Carry Advantage Ahead of ECB
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1647, hovering between its 20-day SMA at 1.1619 and 200-day SMA at 1.1638. The Fed rate of 3.75% against the ECB rate of 2.4% maintains a 135bp nominal yield advantage in favor of USD, while €STR at 2.19% versus SOFR at 3.65% reflects a 146bp OIS carry discount on holding EUR. CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain a net short EUR position of -52,784 contracts (pctl 31, z -0.39). ECB holds at 2.4%. With 1M 25d risk reversals flat at -0.21, the options market exhibits little appetite to chase euro upside. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent 146bp OIS carry penalty caps sustainable advances above 1.1700. Catalyst: ECB interest rate announcement and monetary policy statement today at 12:15 UTC. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish forward policy path that forces a decisive move through the 200-day SMA at 1.1638.
evidence: EUR/USD OIS carry: SOFR 3.65% vs ESTR 2.19% (146bp)
